Composed of narrow strips of a uniform warp-faced pattern using trans-Saharan alaari handspun magenta silk, interspersed with narrow stripes of white and indigo handspun cotton; the weft is of cotton dyed indigo. A pocket has been sewn to the front, and both front and back have been embroidered in white local silk. The embroidery is in the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern, using chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch; there is a large spiral at the front and another on the back. The knives themselves are embroidered on top of extra pieces of cloth that have been cut to shape and couched down. The tunic appears to be lined with strips of white cotton.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga), hand-woven from hand-spun white cotton. The body is formed of 103 narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. The body of the gown is rectangular in shape, while the sleeves are wider at the top than at the bottom and so flare out at the top. At the front is sewn a large pocket. The gown is hand-embroidered in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern. The two knives and the area around the neck are embroidered with a cream coloured local silk thread; the rest of the decoration (five squares and two spirals (tambari), one on the front and one on the back) are in the same white cotton as the body of the gown, and are in chain and buttonhole eyelet stitching. The sleeves of the garment are sewn with a hem; the neck and bottom are not.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Man's gown (tobe, boubou, riga saki). The body is formed of 179 narrow strips, hand-woven from hand-spun indigo-dyed cotton of two shades which produce a mottled effect; the strips are hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are uniform and use indigo-dyed cotton in both warp and weft, with lines of white cotton inserted frequently and regularly in both warp and weft to create a checked appearance of a blue/grey colour (known as ‘saki’ by the Hausa’ and ‘etu’ by the Yoruba). The sleeves are wider at the top than the bottom and as a result fan out. At the front is sewn an exceptionally large pocket. The pocket, shoulder and front are hand-embroidered in white cotton in a large rectangle that extends beyond the pocket . The embroidery is in chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch, and in the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern; there is a large spiral at the front and another smaller one on the back. The knives themselves are embroidered on top of extra pieces of cloth that have been cut to shape. The edges of the neck and sleeves have not been lined.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga). The body is formed of 49 uniform strips, hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges; each strip has three broad stripes of hand-spun magenta (alaari) silk separated by narrower bands of machine-spun European white and yellow cotton; the weft is indigo, which gives the alaari a purple tinge. Four gussets of locally-spun and woven white cotton are inserted along the skirt of the main body in order to make the skirt flare; the sleeves are wider at the top than the bottom and as a result fan out. At the front is sewn a large pocket. The pocket, shoulder and front are hand-embroidered in European green thread with the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern in chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch; there is a small spiral at the front and another on the back. Along the inside at the bottom of the gown is a lining of European printed cotton with a 'paisley' boteh motif printed in black, blue and white, and with a background in red. All the edges have a hand-sewn hem.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe) made from four sheets of European cotton sheeting, cut and dyed in indigo in Africa, and sewn together into a rectangular gown with square sleeves. At the front is added an irregularly shaped pocket of the same material. Both the front and the back are extensively embroidered with hand-sewn decoration in white, green, red, light blue, dark blue, and yellow European cotton thread, in patterns that include knives, stars and spirals. The decoration on the front is asymmetrical; that on the back is symmetrical. One side of the neck aperture is lined with red braid. The sleeves and base are hemmed by machine.
